articleTitle: Homeomorphism and diffeomorphism classification of Eschenburg spaces
The Fesenko groups have finite width
abstract: We examine the lower central series of the so-called Fesenko groups T=T(r). These are a certain class of closed subgroups of the Nottingham Group. It is known that all such T are hereditarily just infinite for p>2. Here we establish that T has finite width, adding to the list of known examples. We also prove that T has infinite obliquity.

articleTitle: Bounded linear Talagrand operators on ordinal spaces
abstract: In this paper we prove results concerning linear Talagrand operators, including a complete solution to the existence or otherwise of such operators on C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(L), where L=∏<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i=1</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>[0,Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) is a product of ordinal spaces endowed with the locally compact order topology.

articleTitle: Zero–infinity laws in Diophantine approximation
abstract: It is shown that for any translation invariant outer measure M, the M-measure of the intersection of any subset of R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> that is invariant under rational translations and which does not have full Lebesgue measure with the closure of an open set of positive measure cannot be positive and finite. Analogues for p-adic fields and fields of formal power series over a finite field are established. The results are applied to some problems in metric Diophantine approximation.

articleTitle: Trace fields of representations and virtually Haken 3-manifolds
abstract: We introduce and study trace fields and invariant trace fields of SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(C) and PSL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(C) representations of 3-manifold groups. We give conditions on such fields which imply that the underlying 3-manifold is virtually Haken or has virtually positive or ∞ first Betti number. In particular, we define the notion of an algebraically trace-proper surface subgroup in a 3-manifold group, and show that any closed orientable irreducible 3-manifold with such a surface subgroup is virtually Haken. We give infinitely many families of closed orientable hyperbolic non-Haken 3-manifolds with algebraically trace-proper surface subgroups.

articleTitle: Stable moment mappings and singular lagrangian Fibrations
abstract: We study singular Lagrangian fibrations given by moment mappings using cohomological methods. We give a theorem for the stability of these foliations and construct a symplectic version of Mather's stable mapping theorem.

articleTitle: Induction and Decomposition Numbers for RoCK Blocks
abstract: This work is concerned with RoCK blocks (also known as Rouquier blocks) of symmetric groups. A RoCK block, b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ,w</inf>, with abelian defect group is Morita equivalent to a certain block of a wreath product of symmetric group algebras (Chuang and Kessar). Turner specified an idempotent, e, and conjectured that, for arbitrary weight w, eb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ,w</inf>e should be Morita equivalent to this block of the wreath product. In this work we provide evidence in support of this conjecture. We prove that the decomposition matrices of these two algebras are identical. As a corollary to the proof, we obtain some knowledge of the composition factors of induced and restricted simple modules.

articleTitle: Quantum complete rings and blocks with one simple module
abstract: We generalize a construction of Benson and Green to realize a large class of quantum complete intersections as basic algebras of non-principal blocks of certain finite groups. The realization arises from an isomorphism of a quantum complete ring to a skew group ring. We also show that blocks of finite groups with normal abelian defect groups, abelian inertial quotients and, up to isomorphism, only one simple module have basic algebras amongst this class of quantum complete intersections. We also study the Ext rings and finite p′-coverings of these quantum complete intersections.

articleTitle: Dirichlet Problems of a Quasi-Linear Elliptic System
abstract: We discuss the Dirichlet problem of the quasi-linear elliptic system−e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−f(U)</sup>div(e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> f(U)</sup>∇U)+½f′(U)|∇U|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0inΩ,U|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∂Ω</inf>=Φ.Here Ω is a smooth bounded domain in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, f:R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>→R is a smooth function, U:Ω→R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> is the unknown vector-valued function, Φ:Ω̄→Rp<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> is a given vector-valued C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,δ</sup> function, and f′ is the gradient of the function f with respect to the variable U. Such problems arise in population dynamics and differential geometry. The difficulty in studying this kind of problem is that this nonlinear elliptic system does not fit the usual growth condition in M. Giaquinta's book of 1983 and the natural working space H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>∩L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>(Ω) for the corresponding Euler–Lagrange functional does not fit the usual minimization or variational argument. We use the direct method on a convex subset of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>∩L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>(Ω) to overcome these difficulties. Under a suitable assumption on the function f, we prove that there is at least one solution to this problem. We also give an application of our result to the Dirichlet problem of harmonic maps into the standard sphere

articleTitle: A splitting result for the free loop space of spheres and projective spaces
abstract: Let X be a 1-connected compact space such that the algebra H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(X;F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is generated by one single element. We compute the cohomology of the free loop space H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(ΛX;F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) including the Steenrod algebra action. When X is a projective space CP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> n</sup>, HP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> n</sup>, the Cayley projective plane CaP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or a sphere S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> we obtain a splitting result for integral and mod two cohomology of the suspension spectrum ∑<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>(ΛX)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf>. The splitting is in terms of ∑<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf> and the Thom spaces Th(qτ), q≥0, of the q-fold Whitney sums of the tangent bundle τ over X.

articleTitle: Conjugators of Fuchsian groups and quasiplatonic surfaces
abstract: Let G be a Fuchsian group containing two torsion free subgroups defining isomorphic Riemann surfaces. Then these surface subgroups K and αKα<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> are conjugate in PSL(2,R), but in general the conjugating element α cannot be taken in G or a finite index Fuchsian extension of G. We will show that in the case of a normal inclusion in a triangle group G these α can be chosen in some triangle group extending G. It turns out that the method leading to this result allows also to answer the question of how many different regular dessins of the same type can exist on a given quasiplatonic Riemann surface.

articleTitle: Operators on σ-complete C*-algebras
abstract: Let B be a unital monotone σ-complete C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebra, X a Banach space and (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) (n=1, 2,…) a sequence of weakly compact operators from B to X. Our key theorem implies that if limT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>p exists for each projection p in B, then there exists a weakly compact operator T such that ‖T″<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(b)−T″(b)‖→0, for each b in B″. (An immediate corollary of this is that B is a Grothendieck space.) Let μ be any state of B such that each T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is strongly absolutely continuous with respect to μ. Then, as a consequence of our key theorem, we obtain the following uniform absolute continuity property. For each ε>0, there exists δ>0, such that, whenever b is in the unit ball of B and μ(bb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>+b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>b)<δ, then ‖T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>b‖≤ε for all n. This last result is a far reaching non-commutative generalization of the classical Brooks–Jewett theorem for vector measures.

articleTitle: Cut vertices in commutative graphs
abstract: The homology of Kontsevich's commutative graph complex parametrizes finite type invariants of odd-dimensional manifolds. This graph homology is also the twisted homology of Outer Space modulo its boundary, so gives a nice point of contact between geometric group theory and quantum topology. In this paper we give two different proofs (one algebraic, one geometric) that the commutative graph complex is quasi-isomorphic to the quotient complex obtained by modding out by graphs with cut vertices. This quotient complex has the advantage of being smaller and hence more practical for computations. In addition, it supports a Lie bialgebra structure coming from a bracket and cobracket we defined in a previous paper. As an application, we compute the rational homology groups of the commutative graph complex up to rank 7.

articleTitle: Scalar curvature and projective embeddings, II
abstract: The main result of the paper is that, under certain hypotheses, a Kahler metric of constant scalar curvature minimises the Mabuchi functional. The method uses finite-dimensional approximations involving projective embeddings.

articleTitle: JC*-Triples and Inner Ideals in Universally Reversible JC*-Algebras
abstract: It is shown that a JC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-triple whose Cartan factor representations all have rank greater than two has a composition series in which successive quotients are isomorphic to inner ideals in a universally reversible JC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebra.

articleTitle: 2-GOOD RINGS
abstract: A ring R is said to be k-good if every element is the sum of k units. We show that the endomorphism ring of a free module of rank at least 2 is 3-good and that every ring can be embedded in a 2-good ring. Answering a question of Skornjakov, we show that a (right) self-injective von Neumann regular ring is 2-good provided it has no 2-torsion. This generalizes a result of Zelinsky's on the ring of linear transformations of a vector space.

articleTitle: Bounds and definability in polynomial rings
abstract: We study questions around the existence of bounds and the dependence on parameters for linear-algebraic problems in polynomial rings over rings of an arithmetic flavour. In particular, we show that the module of syzygies of polynomials f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,… , f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>∈R[X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,… ,X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>] with coefficients in a Prüfer domain R can be generated by elements whose degrees are bounded by a number only depending on N, n and the degree of the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>. This implies that if R is a Bézout domain, then the generators can be parametrized in terms of the coefficients of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,… , f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> using the ring operations and a certain division function, uniformly in R.

articleTitle: The H-Structure of Low-Rank Torsion Free H-Spaces
abstract: Starting with a p-local space X of l odd dimensional cells, l<p−1, Cooke, Harper, and Zabrodsky constructed an H-space Y with the property that H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>(Y) is generated as an exterior Hopf algebra by H̃<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>(X). Cohen and Neisendorfer, and later Selick and Wu, reproduced this result with different constructions. We use the Selick and Wu approach to show that Y is homotopy associative and homotopy commutative if X is a suspension and l<p−2.

articleTitle: Big points in C*-algebras and JB*-triples
abstract: Let X be a Banach space. For a norm-one element u in X we put σ(X, u):=sup{||ψ−Π(ψ)||:ψ∈D(X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">**</sup>, u)}, where D(X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">**</sup>, ·) denotes the duality mapping of X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">**</sup>, and Π : X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">***</sup>→X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> stands for the Dixmier projection. The element u is said to be a big point of X if the closed convex hull of the orbit of u under the group of all surjective isometries on X is the closed unit ball of X. We prove that, if X is either a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebra or the predual of a von Neumann algebra, and if there is a big point u of X with σ(X,u)<2 and such that the norm of X is strongly subdifferentiable at u (in the sense [36]), then X is finite-dimensional, and the big points of X are precisely the extreme points of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>. This is derived from a more general result on JB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-triples and preduals of JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-triples.

articleTitle: On connectedness of the spaCe of harmonic 2-spheres in Lagrangian Grassmann manifolds
abstract: The Lagrangian Grassmann manifold LG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is a non-inner symmetric space that plays an important role in many mathematical and physical problems. The purpose of this paper is to study the deformations of harmonic maps of S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> into LG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, which are strongly isotropic or real mixed pairs. As a consequence, we obtain the results on the connectedness of the spaces of such harmonic 2‐spheres in LG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>.

articleTitle: Mean square estimate for twisted automorphic L-functions on weight aspect
abstract: We study the mean square estimate for the twisted automorphic L-functions averaged over Hecke eigencuspforms at large weight. The upper bound obtained is quite sharp, and a direct application yields an unconditional version for a result of Kohnen and Sengupta.

articleTitle: Values of arithmetical functions equal to a sum of two squares
abstract: Let φ(n) denote the Euler function. In this paper, we determine the order of growth for the number of positive integers n≤x for which φ(n) is the sum of two square numbers. We also obtain similar results for the Dedekind function ψ(n) and the sum of divisors function σ(n).

articleTitle: Lie powers in prime degree
abstract: Let L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V) denote the pth Lie power of a finite-dimensional module V for a group G over a field of prime characteristic p, where L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V) is regarded as a submodule of the tensor power T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V). There is a natural homomorphism from L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V) onto the pth metabelian Lie power M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V). We show that the kernel of this homomorphism is a direct summand of T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V) and apply this result to the generic case where G is the general linear group on V and the field is infinite. In this case we find the indecomposable direct summands of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(V) and their multiplicities.

articleTitle: Theta function identities and Ramanujan's Congruences on the partition function
abstract: A q-difference equation on eight shifted factorials of infinite order will be established. As consequences, we shall systematically explore triple products to give alternative proofs of the theta function identities due to Ewell [5, 6] and Berndt et al. [2] and briefly review their applications to the Ramanujan congruences on the partition function. In particular, a q-difference equation on quintuple products will be discovered which leads us to a new representation of (q;q)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> and therefore a new proof of the Ramanujan congruence on the partition function modulo 11.

articleTitle: Symplectic fibrations and Riemann–Roch numbers of reduced spaces
abstract: In this article we give formulae for the Riemann–Roch number of a symplectic quotient arising as the reduced space of a coadjoint orbit O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Λ</inf> (for Λ∈g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> close to 0) as an evaluation of cohomology classes over the reduced space at 0. Such a formula exhibits the dependence of the Riemann–Roch number on Λ. We also express the formula as a sum over the components of the fixed point set of the maximal torus. Our proof applies to Hamiltonian G-manifolds even if they do not have a compatible Kähler structure, using the definition of quantization in terms of the Spin-C Dirac operator.

articleTitle: Erratum
On the dentability of weak*-Hδ sets
abstract: We state several conditions equivalent to weak<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-dentability for certain subsets of a dual Banach space which include both the compact case and a result of Ghoussoub and Maurey.

articleTitle: Norms on rings and the Hilbert scheme of points on the line
abstract: We generalize the algebraic results of Laksov and Skjelnes (2001) and Skjelnes (2002), and obtain easy and transparent proofs of the representability of the Hilbert functor of points on the affine scheme whose coordinate ring is any localization of the polynomial ring in one variable over an arbitrary base ring. The coordinate ring of the Hilbert scheme is determined. We also make explicit the relation between our methods and the beautiful treatment of the Hilbert scheme of curves via norms, indicated by Grothendieck (1995), and performed by Deligne (1973).

articleTitle: The range and kernel inclusion of algebraic derivations and commuting maps
abstract: Let δ and δ′ be derivations of an algebra A. Consider the following conditions: (i) the range of δ′ is contained in the range of δ, (ii) the kernel of δ is contained in the kernel of δ′, (iii) δ is an inner derivation generated by a ∈ A and δ′ is an inner derivation generated by a polynomial in a. If δ is algebraic then we show that under rather mild additional assumptions these three conditions are closely related. This is used in obtaining some new characterizations of commuting maps on certain rings and normed algebras.

articleTitle: Spin spaces and positive decomposition of linear maps on ordered Banach spaces
abstract: Spin factors and generalizations are used to revisit positive generation of B(E, F), where E and F are ordered Banach spaces. Interior points of B(E, F)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf> are discussed and in many cases it is seen that positive generation of B(E, F) is controlled by spin structure in F when F is a JBW-algebra.

articleTitle: Quasi-hereditary quotients of finite Chevalley groups and Frobenius kernels
abstract: Let G be a semisimple connected simply connected linear algebraic group over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0. Denote by G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> its nth Frobenius kernel and by G(p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>) its finite subgroup of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pn</inf>-rational points. In this paper we find quotients of the algebra U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> = k[G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> and of the group algebra kG(p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>) whose module category is equivalent to a (highest weight) subcategory of the category of rational G-modules.

articleTitle: On the unit sum number of some rings
abstract: The unit sum number, u(R), of a ring R is the least k such that every element is the sum of k units; if there is no such k then u(R) is ω or ∞ depending whether the units generate R additively or not. We show that if R is the ring of integers of a quadratic or complex cubic number field then u(R) ≥ ω, in the quadratic case u(R) is completely determined. We also investigate tensor products of algebras. If the ground field is not the field of two elements then their unit sum number is 2 when at least one of them is algebraic and at least ω when neither is algebraic and one of them is pure transcendental.

articleTitle: On boundary spatial embeddings of a graph
abstract: A spatial embedding of a graph is called a ∂-spatial embedding if all knots in the embedding bound Seifert surfaces simultaneously such that the interiors of the surfaces are mutually disjoint and disjoint from the image of the embedding. This is a generalization of the boundary link. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of a graph which has a ∂-spatial embedding and we classify ∂-spatial embeddings completely up to self pass-moves and ambient isotopies. In particular, any ∂-spatial embedding of a graph is trivial up to edge-homotopy.

articleTitle: Nonlinear commutativity preserving maps on self-adjoint operators
abstract: We characterize the bijective nonlinear maps of the set of all self-adjoint bounded linear operators on a complex separable Hilbert space H of dimension at least 3 which preserve commutativity in both directions. Roughly speaking, a bijective map has this property if, and only if, up to a unitary or antiunitary transformation of H, it leaves fixed the self-adjoint parts of the commutative von Neumann algebras on H.

articleTitle: Rigidity theorems for closed hypersurfaces in space forms
abstract: In this paper, we obtain some metric and topological rigidity theorems for closed hypersurfaces in space forms.

articleTitle: Decomposition of tensor products of modular irreducibles for SL2
abstract: We use tilting modules to study the structure of the tensor product of two simple modules for the algebraic group SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, in positive characteristic, obtaining a twisted tensor product theorem for its indecomposable direct summands. Various other related results are obtained, and numerous examples are computed.

articleTitle: C1-fine approximation of functions on Banach spaces with unconditional basis
abstract: We show that if X is a Banach space having an unconditional basis and a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-smooth Lipschitz bump function, then for every C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-smooth function f from X into a Banach space Y, and for every continuous function ε : X → (0, ∞), there exists a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-smooth function g : X → Y such that ‖f − g‖ ≤ ε and ‖f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup> − g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>‖ ≤ ε.

articleTitle: Unconditionality in spaces of m-homogeneous polynomials
abstract: Let E be a Banach space with an unconditional basis. We prove that for m ≥ 2 the Banach space P(<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>E) of all m-homogeneous polynomials on E has an unconditional basis if and only if E is finite dimensional. This answers a problem of S. Dineen.

articleTitle: A group of self homotopy equivalences of SO(4)
abstract: The author determines the group of homotopy classes of self homotopy equivalences of the rotation group of degree 4 which induce the identity on homotopy groups.

articleTitle: A maximal theorem for holomorphic semigroups
abstract: Let X be a closed linear subspace of the Lebesgue space L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(Ω; μ) for some 1 < p < ∞, and let − A be an invertible operator that is the generator of a bounded holomorphic semigroup T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> on X. Then for each 0 < α < 1 the maximal function sup<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t>0</inf> |T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>f(x)| belongs to L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(Ω; μ) for each f in the domain of A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sup>. If moreover iA generates a bounded C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-group and A has spectrum contained in (0, ∞), then A has a bounded H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> functional calculus.

articleTitle: Perturbation methods and first-order partial differential equations on Riemannian manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we give explicit estimates that ensure the existence of solutions for first-order partial differential operators on compact manifolds, using a viscosity method. In the linear case, an explicit integral formula can be found, using the characteristic curves. The solution is given explicitly on the critical points and the limit cycles of the vector field of the first-order term of the operator. In the nonlinear case, a generalization of the Weitzenböck formula provides pointwise estimates that ensure the existence of a solution, but the uniqueness question is left open. Nevertheless we prove that uniqueness is stable under a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> perturbation. Finally, we give some examples where the solution fails to exist globally, justifying the need to impose conditions that guarantee global existence. The final result reveals that the zero-order term in the first-order operator is necessary to obtain generically bounded solutions.

articleTitle: Dead end words in lamplighter groups and other wreath products
abstract: We explore the geometry of the Cayley graphs of the lamplighter groups and a wide range of wreath products. We show that these groups have dead end elements of arbitrary depth with respect to their natural generating sets. An element w in a group G with finite generating set X is a dead end element if no geodesic ray from the identity to w in the Cayley graph Γ(G,X) can be extended past w. Additionally, we describe some non-convex behaviour of paths between elements in these Cayley graphs and seesaw words, which are potential obstructions to these graphs satisfying the k-fellow traveller property.

articleTitle: Quantized trace rings
abstract: The general linear group acts on m-tuples of N×N matrices by simultaneous conjugation. Quantum deformations of the corresponding rings of invariants and the so-called trace rings are investigated in the context of corepresentation theory of the quantum special linear group.
